assets.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset type: one transparent game damage-overlay sprite for a square enamel arcade enemy, NOT a complete enemy. Reference image: the existing 3-stage crack atlas; the RIGHTMOST cell is the old heavy stage which is now being promoted to MEDIUM. Create ONE new square HEAVY overlay that is much more visibly damaged than that rightmost reference cell. Retain the same dark charcoal recessed fractures and slim warm ivory bevel highlights, but roughly triple the visible damaged area: several broad branching cracks, substantial chipped corner wedges, and connected jagged fissures along all four edge bands. It should read as badly battered at 32 pixels, with strong dark shapes rather than tiny hairline scratches. Keep the central 40% by 40% square entirely transparent so the enemy type symbol remains readable. Fractures may reach inward to that clear center boundary, but no marks in the center. Keep the outermost 5% gutter transparent, no flying debris. Aim for damage occupying 12–18% of the whole square, concentrated in the perimeter band; more obvious than the old heavy while preserving the colored enemy beneath. Draw only cracks and small missing-enamel chips floating on genuine transparent alpha. No solid tile, no enemy, no rim frame, no label, no text, no grid, no checkerboard. One square canvas with one overlay, centered and registered to the full square footprint, ideally 1024x1024. Match the crisp illustrated beveled-enamel material of the reference, not rough pixel art.

assets.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: transparent 3-stage DAMAGE OVERLAY atlas for the dragon's round red tracking fireball in a top-down arcade game. Image 1 is the existing fireball to layer over: a red glowing circular orb. Keep that projectile separate, do NOT draw the red orb itself. Image 2 shows square-enemy damage for the general crisp arcade finish only; DO NOT reuse square corner cracks or metallic tile bevels. Draw only ROUND fireball-appropriate damage: curved charcoal scorched fissures and broken cooling crust ribbons with thin hot orange/cream ember lips, following a spherical surface, visibly losing cohesion. Three equal square cells side by side in a 3:1 atlas. Every cell contains one centered circular arrangement occupying a disk of radius 40% of the cell width. All pixels outside that disk and all space between the marks must be truly transparent. LEFT light: two short curved soot cuts on upper-left/lower-right sides of the orb. MIDDLE medium: extend those and add several short branching burned fissures, clearly visible at 32px. RIGHT heavy: substantial broken curved bands and broad blackened fissures distributed around the orb, roughly double medium coverage, unmistakably weakened; orange ember edges keep them readable. Leave the central 20% diameter disk transparent throughout to preserve the bright red core underneath. Keep an identical position and scale in all cells; damage builds from the same marks, no detached debris, no flames extending outside the circular footprint. Match a colorful crisp arcade game, not photorealism; bold shapes and minimal fine detail. No full ring outline, no square corners, no enemy face, no red fill or opaque backing, no text, no labels, no frames, no checkerboard. Transparent background. Render a horizontal 3:1 atlas, ideally 1536x512.
